cards.explanation: The answer is army. God says He will "…bring you out with all your army…" and then lists horses, horsemen in full armor, shields, bucklers and swords. That's a whole lot of gear for one prince, friends. I can barely get my cookie boxes stacked straight. (Ezekiel 38:4)

The answer is True. God says, "Get ready; prepare yourself, you and all your company gathered around you…" It's a call to get set, and it takes in the whole company, not just Gog. Me, I get ready by hunting for my apron, and I've never needed a company for that. (Ezekiel 38:7)

The answer is people gathered from many nations. God says the land has people "…gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate." So a place that sat empty for a long time has people living in it again. Sounds like a bakery that finally got its lights back on, friends. (Ezekiel 38:8)

The answer is False. God says the people were brought out from the nations and "…all now dwell securely." They're settled and at ease, not living in fear, friends. That calm is what Gog will later point to when he makes his plan. (Ezekiel 38:8)

The answer is an evil plan. God says, "On that day, thoughts will arise in your mind, and you will devise an evil plan." The thoughts show up first, and then the scheme takes shape. I've had thoughts show up in my head too, friends, but mine were mostly about extra chocolate chips. (Ezekiel 38:10)

The answer is that they live without walls or gates. Gog says he will come against "…a land of unwalled villages…" and a quiet people, "…all of them living without walls or bars or gates…" Those are his own words about the people he plans to attack. I think he sees a place with no defenses and starts counting the plunder, friends. (Ezekiel 38:11)

The answer is True. Gog says he will go "…in order to seize the spoil and carry off the plunder…" Those words are part of the plan God says Gog will speak in verse 12. He says it plainly, about the quiet land, friends. (Ezekiel 38:12)

The answer is False. God says Gog will come "…from your place out of the far north…" with many peoples. They're all riding horses. The direction God gives is north, not south, friends. (Ezekiel 38:15)

The answer is so the nations may know Him. God says, "…so that the nations may know Me when I show Myself holy in you before their eyes." It's about the nations seeing who He is. Gog is coming, friends, but God is the one in charge of the whole thing. (Ezekiel 38:16)

The answer is prophets. God asks if Gog is the one "…of whom I have spoken in former days through My servants, the prophets of Israel…" So God's question points back to what He spoke in former days through the prophets. The text says they prophesied for years in those times, friends. (Ezekiel 38:17)

The answer is True. God says, "Now on that day when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, My wrath will flare up." It's a heavy line, so I'll say it plainly, friends. The timing is the point: it's on the very day Gog comes against the land. (Ezekiel 38:18)

The answer is every creature and all mankind. God says the fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the field, every creature that crawls on the ground and "…all mankind on the face of the earth will tremble at My presence." That's the sea, the sky and the ground all in one list. Nothing in that list is left out, friends. (Ezekiel 38:20)

The answer is False. God says the mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and "…every wall will fall to the ground." That's mountains, cliffs and walls, all coming down, friends. It's a heavy picture of how big this earthquake is. (Ezekiel 38:19-20)

The answer is his own brother. God says, "And I will summon a sword against Gog on all My mountains, declares the Lord GOD, and every man’s sword will be against his brother." It's a heavy line, friends. The swords are turned on brothers. (Ezekiel 38:21)

The answer is his troops and the nations with him. God says He will pour out torrents of rain, hailstones, fire and sulfur "…on him and on his troops and on the many nations with him." So it falls on Gog and everyone who came along, friends. This is a heavy part, and God is the one doing it. (Ezekiel 38:22)
